notes:
Passed on the fake backend by `python3 -m mhs.driver check MHS/drivers/labs/aicell-lab__hamilton-control --backend fake` (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level); G1-G9 passed with no findings and no warnings. `gate.digest` is the digest the last check printed; check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not hand-edited. The package is model-authored (driver.lock.json authored_by kind model, model_id deepseek-v4.1-flash:1017, run_id helper-wave-1-027) and unreviewed (reviewed_by null); no human reviewed or tested it; no hardware was attached, no hardware backend was run, and no hardware or upstream-simulator run is claimed. The fake is an in-memory stand-in, not a recording.

SHAPE AND DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card names helper PyLabRobotDriver and decision family-config. That helper serves only a PyLabRobot LiquidHandler front end (the exemplar README and MHS/sdk/docs/pylabrobot-helper.md), and the selected entry is the card's concrete entry symbol pylabrobot.incubators.incubator:Incubator (pylabrobot/incubators/incubator.py:23), which is not a LiquidHandler. This package is therefore a direct Driver over Incubator (DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: direct Driver, not PyLabRobotDriver). The card's hints name Incubator temperature, shaking and plate-transfer methods, and the clone contains both the front end and the Cytomat serial backend. The card's entry symbols do not include the Vantage class named by README.md:3 and used by try.py:4-5; the Hamilton Vantage has no native motion stop (HamiltonLiquidHandler.stop only fails waiting tasks and clears the queue, base.py:98-102; Vantage subclasses it, vantage.py:342), so a hardware Vantage package could not meet SAFE-045 without inventing a stop. This package therefore does not claim Vantage liquid-handling control; it drives the concrete Incubator front end that the card also lists.

SAFETY: risk R2 because the device shakes and moves plates. The @estop method calls Incubator.stop_shaking and then de-energizes the deployment's independent power-cut relay; the safe_state=True action x-cap.aicell-lab.safe_stop.v1 runs the same path and is the safe_state.achieved_by binding. The hardware factory native.py requires options['safe_stop'] and refuses without it; the fake uses a no-op placeholder relay. No estop_physical_ref and no vendor e-stop are claimed. The loader refuses the hardware backend of this unreviewed model-authored R2 package before the factory runs, so the fake run does not establish a hardware stop. Machine.stop is only the lifecycle teardown and is not used as the stop (machine.py:67-70). The upstream Incubator exposes no heater-off; Cytomat.set_temperature raises NotImplementedError (cytomat.py:370-371), so the independent relay is required for the thermal hazard. The fake's safe state stops shaking; it treats the relay as a no-op placeholder and does not model the relay physically. The door is not part of the safe state; open_door and close_door are not exposed as actions.

LIMITS: the clone states no temperature or shaking range for a deployed incubator, so cap.thermal.setpoint.v1 target_temperature and x-cap.aicell-lab.start_shaking.v1 frequency use Limit.operator_required. Without an operator overlay every call is refused MHS.SAFETY.LIMITS_UNSET. site-limits.example.json is an illustrative operator overlay only (4-40 Cel, 0.1-5 Hz); those numbers are examples, not facts or device bounds. No bound was copied from a catalogue class default or an upstream constructor default.

FAKE AND COVERAGE: the fake implements only Incubator's public methods (G7 passed) and models temperature, shaking, door state, free-site count, fetch and take-in. Its plate names, temperature, free-site count and loading-tray queue are placeholders. It is not a recording and has no motion, timing, thermal or serial model; it treats the independent relay as a no-op and, on a fresh gate endpoint with no preceding fetch, auto-presents a site plate to take_in_plate (the real Incubator expects a plate already on the loading tray). The fake was not compared with the upstream Incubator or the Cytomat serial protocol. NOT COVERED: the Hamilton Vantage liquid handler and its pipetting, 96-head, iSWAP and gripper paths; the Cytomat serial transport, barcode, CO2, humidity, O2 and error registers; open_door and close_door as separate actions; take_in_plate's PlateHolder argument (only random and smallest are exposed); set_temperature on the default Cytomat backend (it raises NotImplementedError; a deployment backend implementing the IncubatorBackend interface is required for temperature control); a hardware run.

FACTS: every Fact cites a line or span of the clone at a857bd9a1f91d140a90d6a2cd29b01c50b23106a, and G4 passed with no REF_VALUE or REF_BINARY warnings. README.md:3 states the project controls the Hamilton Vantage, and try.py:4-5 builds the LiquidHandler over Vantage; those facts document the repository, not this package's selected device. The Incubator facts are read from incubator.py:23-152, cytomat.py:359-371, machine.py:67-70, base.py:98-102 and vantage.py:342.

LICENSE AND INSTALL: the card records license_spdx NOASSERTION; the clone has no LICENSE file (README.md says MIT and refers to a LICENSE file that is absent), so this package claims no licence. The card's install block has no commands; the hardware factory needs the clone installed plus deployment options and was never run. task.json is unchanged. The clone was not modified, imported, installed or run; only the gate read it. All files are English.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked the direct-Driver deviation, the scope and the stop against README.md, try.py and the vendored PyLabRobot copy. The repository's device is the Hamilton Vantage liquid handler (README.md:3, try.py:4-5), whose vendored backend has no stop command (HamiltonLiquidHandler.stop only fails waiting tasks, base.py:98-102; no abort in vantage.py), as the readiness evidence predicted. The author instead served the vendored PyLabRobot Incubator front end (Cytomat backend), library code no repository file uses, and bound as e-stop and safe_state=True action stop_shaking plus options['safe_stop'], a 'deployment-supplied independent power-cut relay' callable that no line of the clone shows and the fake made a no-op, so the SDK reported an achieved safe state for an invented stop; the served temperature setpoint cannot work with the only concrete backend (Cytomat.set_temperature raises NotImplementedError, cytomat.py:370-371) while the fake applies it at once. The reviewer removed the relay (driver.py, native.py), made the e-stop send stop_shaking and then raise SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED, turned the safe-stop action into an ordinary x-cap.aicell-lab.stop_shaking.v1 (driver.py, fixtures/conformance.json), made the e-stop case expect SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED with the latch held (test_driver.py), added a review section to facts.md and regenerated reference.json and REFERENCE.md. The gate now fails G3 (R2 hardware without an acknowledged stop or safe-state action; stable digest sha256:2171d0c023358d9a5101616b41e60b2291153d7f5383307bb362dbad6cfd8323); the author's pass and notes on the relay stop are superseded. The card needs the owner's publication decision (publish_review required; licence not stated (NOASSERTION)); the package may not be published or merged into a published tree before it. For the human reviewer: A real package would drive the Vantage (R2 pipetting and gantry motion) and needs a source-backed stop or a human-cited physical stop, plus an entry-symbol override: the card's five entries (Incubator, EVO, CytomatChatterbox, OpentronsBackend, HTTPBackend) are vendored PyLabRobot classes, none of them the Vantage. The README says MIT, but the clone has no LICENSE file.
